correctness.rationale: The previously established classification of all maximal class-<=k nilpotent subsemigroups by ordered k-layer partitions is explicitly separated from the new optimization. For a fixed ordered layer vector, an element is exactly a partial injection with all arrows strictly increasing in layer number; its rank is the number of arrows. Decompose the injection into directed chains; after forgetting direction each chain is a block meeting each layer at most once, and conversely sorting block colors supplies a unique increasing chain. This is a rank-preserving bijection to colored transversal set partitions and proves the EGF coefficient formula. Recolor a marked item between two layer sizes a>=b+2 while tracking h blocks meeting both colors; the exact ratio (b+1)(a-h)/[a(b+1-h)] >=1 in each rank/block stratum, with strict inequality when h>=1. Every intermediate imbalance is improved, and rank-one strictness excludes unbalanced maximizers. An independent direct enumeration of all partial injections for ordered layers up to n=6 matched the distinct transversal-partition recurrence and coefficientwise inequalities. The enumeration is a test, not a proof for arbitrary n,k.
residual_risks: Use of the prior classification theorem for all maximal class-<=k subsemigroups is essential and independently checked against its actual source; enumeration through n=6 is not a universal certificate.

Earlier 1994/1995 direct classification papers are not fully compared and remain a concrete priority risk.

value.rationale: Maximal cardinality at a fixed nilpotency class is a natural extremal invariant in finite transformation semigroups. A rank-preserving chain/partition bijection and simultaneous coefficientwise inequality settle every bounded class k>=3, the complete rank polynomial and all maximizing ordered-layer shapes, beyond a k=2 textbook balancing computation.
residual_risks: Some formulas can be generated by a standard exponential formula, but the strict, rank-by-rank balancing classification is the substantive new step.

limitations: n>=k>=3 and inclusion of the empty partial map as zero; prior general maximal-class classification explicitly assumed.
Historical pre-2005 layered semigroup extremal literature not exhaustively assessed.
